# Preseason Projection Audit — 2025 & 2026

**Date**: 2026-05-29
**Inputs**: 495 team-seasons (2025 n=263, 2026 n=232) scored by Phase B
projection (LOSO roster-impact model + LOSO trajectory OOF + LOCO
freshman OOF), blended 0.50·baseline + 0.50·raw with offset 0.
**Generated by**: `training/audit_preseason_projections.py` →
`preseason_audit_20260529_summary.json`.

## Headline

| Model                  | MAE  | Bias  | RMSE | R²    |
| ---------------------- | ---- | ----- | ---- | ----- |
| Phase B blended (live) | 5.88 | −0.09 | 7.36 | 0.803 |
| Phase B raw            | 6.44 | +0.63 | 8.01 | 0.766 |
| Baseline-persistence   | 6.53 | −0.81 | 8.28 | 0.750 |

Matches the documented LOSO pooled MAE (5.88) — the live page is being
served the model we measured.

## Honesty findings

**All three model components in the projection pipeline are leak-free at
the season level for this backtest:**

- **Roster-impact (Phase B)**: leave-one-season-out per the LOSO export
  pipeline in `train_roster_impact_model.py` (`models/roster_impact_loso/
  roster_impact_model_{year}.onnx`). The backtest loads the per-target
  model so the impact calibrator never sees its target.
- **Trajectory**: the `leave_one_pair_out` function in
  `train_trajectory_model.py` is misnamed — it holds out each unique
  `(s_n, s_np1)` pair, which is exactly leave-one-target-season-out at
  the pair level. The predictions persisted to
  `trajectory_oof_predictions` (consumed by the backtest) ARE those LOSO
  predictions. **LOSO pooled MAE 2.133 vs 5-fold MAE 2.130 — tight, no
  season-level memorization.**
- **Freshman**: leave-one-class-out per `train_freshman_model.py`. OOF
  written to `freshman_oof_predictions`, consumed verbatim in the
  backtest.

No retraining needed for honesty — the projection pipeline is structurally
honest. **The remaining 5.88 MAE is honest signal-to-noise, not leakage.**

(My initial concern was that the trajectory model's k-fold OOF would be
the leakage channel for a 2026 backtest. The naming `leave_one_pair_out`
is what threw me — it's not row-level LOPO, it's season-level LOSO. Doc
in the trajectory training script could be sharper about this.)

## Where the projection fails (per-bucket bias)

By **actual AdjEM** quartile — this is the load-bearing finding:

| Bucket               | n   | MAE  | Bias  | Baseline MAE | Interpretation                                    |
| -------------------- | --- | ---- | ----- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Q1 bottom (worst)    | 124 | 7.05 | +6.09 | 6.60         | **Over-projects bad teams by 6 AdjEM** on average |
| Q2 below-median      | 124 | 4.88 | −0.79 | 6.27         | Best bucket; mild under-projection                |
| Q3 above-median      | 123 | 5.73 | −1.32 | 7.00         | Mild under-projection                             |
| Q4 top (best)        | 124 | 5.87 | −4.35 | 6.24         | **Under-projects top teams by 4 AdjEM** on average |

Classic regression-to-mean signature. The global slope test (OLS
`actual = a + b·blended`) returns b=1.051 (|t vs 1.0|=2.18), intercept
near zero — predictions are roughly unbiased *on average*, but the
slope > 1 means the predicted range is narrower than the actual range
(i.e., projections are compressed relative to reality). The
**conditional-on-actual** binning is what exposes the structure:
predictions cluster too narrowly around the center mass; the tails of
the actual distribution are under-served.

Applying the implied linear de-shrinkage (`corrected = a + b·blended`)
only buys +0.05 MAE because most teams sit near the center where the
correction is small. The per-quartile bias at the tails is much larger
than what a linear rescale captures, suggesting the pred↔actual
relationship is **non-linear at the tails**. **The fix has to come from
better tail features**, not a global rescale.

By **returning-minutes share** (continuity proxy):

| Bucket            | n   | MAE  | Bias  |
| ----------------- | --- | ---- | ----- |
| Q1 low-return     | 124 | 5.98 | +0.29 |
| Q2                | 124 | 5.23 | +0.29 |
| Q3                | 123 | 6.42 | −1.06 |
| Q4 high-return    | 124 | 5.91 | +0.11 |

**Flat across buckets.** The "sticky last year" theory the ROADMAP §6
candidates list bet on does not show up — returning-share is not a
missing signal. Defer the "returning-experience weight" candidate.

## Residual signal hunt (OLS, standardized signals → signed error)

R² = 0.052 (the signals collectively explain ~5% of projection error —
most error is irreducible). Significant features (|t| > 2):

| Signal                  | β std  | t     | Interpretation                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `portal_outbound_cam_v3`| +0.978 | +2.53 | **Teams losing high-cam_v3 players are over-projected** |

Notable but not significant at p<0.05:

| Signal                  | β std  | t     | Interpretation                                          |
| ----------------------- | ------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `recruit_count`         | −0.987 | −1.56 | More incoming recruits → under-projected (top programs) |
| `portal_inbound_cam_v3` | −0.605 | −1.44 | More incoming portal cam_v3 → under-projected           |
| `recruit_top100_count`  | −0.523 | −1.15 | More top-100 recruits → under-projected                 |

The asymmetry between **outbound** (clearly significant) and **inbound**
(directionally consistent but not significant) tells a story: the
projection pipeline correctly props up arrivals (Phase B aggregates
projected cam_v3 of arrivals, freshman model handles recruits), but
**doesn't fully discount for portal departures**. Teams that lose top
talent end up worse than the model thinks.

## Named cases that anchor the story

**Most over-projected** (predicted high, were actually worse):

| Team               | Season | Pred  | Actual | Err   | Notes                                  |
| ------------------ | ------ | ----- | ------ | ----- | -------------------------------------- |
| Maryland           | 2026   | +25.6 | +5.2   | +20.4 | net_portal=−8 (mass exodus)            |
| South Carolina St. | 2026   | −9.1  | −32.7  | +23.6 | Bottom-of-D-I drift up                 |
| UMKC               | 2026   | −6.1  | −27.0  | +20.9 | Bottom-of-D-I drift up                 |
| UTSA               | 2026   | −1.6  | −21.1  | +19.5 | net_portal=−7                          |

**Maryland 2026 is the cleanest case for the outbound-cam_v3 finding**:
the projection had +25.6 (top-30 team), the team ended at +5.2 (decent
but unremarkable). net_portal=−8 says they lost a lot of players, but
the projection didn't downweight enough.

**Most under-projected** (predicted low, were actually breakouts):

| Team           | Season | Pred  | Actual | Err   | Notes                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | ----- | ------ | ----- | -------------------------------------- |
| Florida        | 2025   | +23.7 | +40.2  | −16.5 | Won the national title                 |
| Auburn         | 2025   | +25.4 | +41.7  | −16.3 | #1 seed                                |
| Missouri       | 2025   | +8.7  | +28.5  | −19.8 | Coaching change reversal               |
| Maryland       | 2025   | +15.3 | +30.6  | −15.3 | Class chemistry surprise               |
| UC San Diego   | 2025   | +1.6  | +22.2  | −20.6 | First-year D-I breakout                |

These are the surprises our static features can't predict: coaching
turnover, locker-room chemistry, undervalued mid-major recruiting. The
honest framing here is "no projection system catches these without
fundamentally different inputs."

## Recommendations (ordered by expected lift)

1. **Net portal Δ-CamPom as a roster-impact feature** *(highest-confidence
   lift; OLS-significant at p<0.05)*. Currently the Phase B model
   aggregates the *projected* cam_v3 of arrivals + returners + recruits.
   It does not explicitly see the *cam_v3 of departures* — the talent
   that left. A team that retains 90 minutes of −1 cam_v3 vs a team that
   lost 90 minutes of +5 cam_v3 look identical to the model conditional
   on the projected roster's composition. Add `outbound_cam_v3_sum`
   (or `delta_vs_baseline_roster`) as a feature.

2. **Top-tail freshman-impact recalibration** *(directional, large
   absolute residual)*. The recruit-related signals are all in the same
   direction (we under-project teams with strong incoming classes), and
   the worst under-projections are top recruiting programs that
   over-performed. The freshman model's documented selection-bias issue
   for top recruits (`models/freshman_model_meta.json::loco_cv`) flows
   into Phase B. Worth quantifying how much of the Q4-bias is
   attributable to freshman-model conservatism — if it's most of it,
   tightening the freshman top-tail is the lever.

3. **Coaching-change indicator** *(unmeasured; suspected high lift on
   tail residuals)*. Florida 2025, Missouri 2025, Maryland 2026 all
   reflect coaching-driven surprises. No data source for this in the DB
   today. Cheap path: a curated `data/coaching_changes/YYYY.json` keyed
   by `natstat_id` with a `new_hc_this_offseason: bool` flag, scraped
   once per offseason from Wikipedia/247. Plug into Phase B as a binary
   feature.

4. **Skip "returning-experience weight"** — flat across quartiles, no
   signal. The Phase B aggregator already captures continuity through
   the projected-cam_v3 distribution.

## What this means for the §6 blend work

The audit was framed as a prerequisite for the "Preseason × pit blend"
work. Net read: **the preseason side is good enough to blend with the pit
side**. MAE 5.88 is materially better than the open-Saturday in-season
pit MAE (~13+), so blending will help early-season predictions. But the
**per-team error has systematic structure on the tails**, and that
structure will propagate into early-season blended predictions unless
recommendations 1–3 land first. Top teams in particular will look weaker
than they are during the first three weeks, simply because the preseason
prior is under-projecting them.

Phase ordering proposed:
- **PR A** (this PR's follow-up): land recommendation #1 (net portal
  Δ-CamPom feature). Retrain Phase B and rerun the audit. Acceptance:
  Q4 bias closes by ≥1.5 AdjEM, pooled MAE drops by ≥0.10.
- **PR B**: investigate freshman-model top-tail recalibration. Audit
  partitions Q4 bias into trajectory-projection error vs roster-impact
  error vs freshman error attribution. Picked from the OLS residual
  decomposition.
- **PR C**: coaching-change ingest. Cheap data, plausibly high lift on
  the residual.
- **Then**: the blend mechanic itself (§6 Phase 3 in the ROADMAP).
